questions.question: To lower the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible. Signal your intentions clearly. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Watch ahead for hazards and be ready to react. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: It is important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if a driver is tailgating you. This warns them that you are about to slow down. It also alerts them to hazards ahead that they may not see. Flash your brake light before slowing in places where drivers do not expect it.

questions.question: In Illinois, a person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.1 percent is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Illinois, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while intoxicated.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is best to:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When rain starts, avoid the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track often works best, but adjust based on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam unless meeting or following another vehicle. Use the headlights of other vehicles to see the road. Wear reflective materials. Choose your lane position flexibly to see well, be seen, and maintain safe space.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a good traction surface, you should:

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will stay under control as long as it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur on trips under five miles long, within a few minutes after starting to ride.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and appear to move more slowly than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their true location and speed.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane usually contains an oily strip. This part of the lane is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of the lane. On dry roads, you can usually ride safely on this strip. When wet, avoid it. The strip is about two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best way to keep ranks close while maintaining an adequate safety cushion is to ride:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets you stay close as a group while keeping safe space between riders. Use single-file in curves, turns, or when entering or leaving highways. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean with them. Sit as close to the operator as possible without crowding them. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance on a motorcycle in normal conditions?
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds of distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead. More space gives you more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags or tie them down. Do not pile loads against a sissy bar or on the seat frame. High loads raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect balance. Spread loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What should you do as you slow down or stop?

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. When stopped, stay in first gear so you can move quickly if you need to.
